subject: MedSys private deployment — security intake & architecture next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Green <alex.green@medsys.com>
Cc: Katie Liu <katie.liu@medsys.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: MedSys private deployment — security intake & architecture next steps

Hi Alex / Katie,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate the clear description of your clinical use case and the compliance constraints. Quick recap and the immediate next steps we discussed so your team has a single place to refer back to.

Summary of compliance posture items we flagged:
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II in-scope for our hosted services; for Private/VPC deployments we provide the same controls and can share our attestation and scoping memo. (Status: attestation available; we will share redacted report and scope doc.)
- HIPAA: Redwood supports signing a BAA for Private deployments. We will propose standard language and can adjust for MedSys legal.
- GDPR/DPA: We provide a DPA for EU data subjects; will include data location and processor subprocessors in the draft.
- Vendor security questionnaire (VSQ): We can kick off your questionnaire — please see attachment "medsys_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx" and a prefilled section where Redwood can accelerate answers.

Private deployment technical notes we discussed:
- Network isolation: VPC peering or private connectivity (Transit/GW) supported; customer-managed VPC preferred.
- Air-gapped option: available as a specialized on-prem package for regulated facilities (longer lead time and airgap runbook required).
- Key management: KMS/HSM integration supported; customer-managed keys recommended for PHI workloads.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs, request traces, and token-level usage are available; retention configurable per contract.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm your primary security contact for the VSQ and timeline for completion (we heard Katie might lead this).
2) Share your network/topology constraints (firewall rules, allowed IP ranges, and whether the deployment needs to be fully air-gapped). If helpful, attach an existing diagram — we attached an initial topology PDF labeled "medsys_vpc_topology_v1.pdf" (draft) for discussion.
3) We propose an architecture workshop to walk through the proposed VPC layout, BAA/DPA items, and operational runbooks. Proposed slots: Thu Feb 12 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri Feb 13 09:00-10:00 PT — let me know which works.

Attachments: medsys_vpc_topology_v1.pdf (draft), medsys_vendor_security_questionnaire.xlsx (prefill)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once I hear which workshop slot works.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: MedSys private deployment — security intake & architecture next steps

Thanks Vanessa — useful recap. A few quick clarifications from our security team (cc'd Katie):

- VSQ: We will start with the questionnaire you attached. Is there a shareable read-only link to a prefilled sheet to avoid email attachments?
- SOC 2: We will need to confirm the exact scope (Prod control plane, data at rest, private deployment host-level controls). Can you indicate whether the SOC 2 includes split control plane components when customers run Private (we have stricter audit requirements)?
- Encryption: For PHI we need TLS1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, and customer-managed KMS (prefer HSM-backed keys). Please confirm Redwood’s support model here.
- Logs / Retention: Our compliance policy requires 7 years of audit log retention for certain PHI events. Can you provide options/costs?

We are leaning toward the private VPC option but need to validate the BAA + the above items. Katie — can you share your availability for the architecture workshop?

Thanks,
Alex
Director of IT Security
MedSys Health
alex.green@medsys.com

Alex / Katie — thanks for the fast replies. Confirming next steps and scheduling the workshop:

1) Architecture workshop: Thu Feb 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite sent to all. Agenda: VPC topology, firewall/IP requirements, KMS/HSM integration, BAA/DPA review, VSQ walkthrough. Please propose changes.

2) VSQ access: I uploaded a prefilled VSQ to a shared Drive folder and set view/comment access for your team: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-medsys-arch. If you prefer a locked sheet, we can give a read-only copy and track changes in a separate column.

3) SOC 2 scope & documentation: Marcus will send the SOC 2 scoping memo by EOD today. We will also provide a redacted attestation and a controls mapping doc.

4) Encryption & KMS: Redwood supports TLS1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and an HSM-backed option for Dedicated/Private. Laura will include pricing options for HSM in her follow-up.

5) Log retention: We have configurable retention; baseline option is 90 days hot, 1 year warm, and archive to Glacier. Laura will include a 7-year archival estimate in the cost options.

6) Air-gapped option: We can run an air-gapped on-prem package — pilot lead time is ~8-12 weeks. We will bring a short runbook to the workshop.

Attached: medsys_vpc_topology_v1.pdf (initial draft). I also attached the VSQ in the Drive folder for edits.

Primary security contact: Katie Liu (katie.liu@medsys.com) — please confirm if that’s correct.

If that's all good I’ll share the SOC 2 scoping memo when Marcus posts it and we’ll review in the workshop. Looking forward to it.

Best,
